title: Work & colleagues
goal: Chat with colleagues, talk to your boss in the right register, handle meetings and deadlines, ask for leave, write a polite work email and get through a job interview.
intro:
A Pakistani office runs on three registers at once: easy, English-heavy chat with colleagues your age (**یار، ڈیڈ لائن کل ہے!**), respectful **آپ** and **سر / میڈم** with anyone senior, and the formal Urdu of notices, letters and HR emails (**آپ کو آگاہ کیا جاتا ہے کہ…**).

This unit gives you all three. The grammar is the **formal register in full** — respect plurals, softening requests with the past tense, formal word swaps — and the **passive** (**فیصلہ کیا گیا** 'it was decided'), which is how official Urdu avoids saying who did what.

grammar.title: The formal register in full
grammar.body:
At work you constantly choose between registers. With colleagues your age: **تم**, plenty of English, یار. With anyone senior, clients and strangers: **آپ** and everything that goes with it.

**1. Respect plurals.** A single respected person takes **plural** verbs and adjectives, even when you talk *about* them: باس آ **گئے** ہیں 'the boss has arrived', میڈم میٹنگ میں **ہیں**، تھوڑی دیر میں **آئیں گی**. Add **صاحب** (men) or **صاحبہ** (women) after a name or title: خان صاحب, مینیجر صاحب. In Pakistani offices **سر** and **میڈم** are used for any senior person, in Urdu as much as in English.

**2. Soften with the past.** A request in the past tense sounds less pushy: مجھے آپ سے بات کرنی **تھی** 'I wanted to have a word with you' (lit. I had to talk), مجھے چھٹی چاہیے **تھی** 'I was hoping for a day off'. Add **ذرا**, **اگر آپ اجازت دیں** 'if you allow', or end with **… ہو سکتا ہے؟** 'would that be possible?'.

**3. Formal word swaps**, especially in writing: بتانا → **آگاہ کرنا / اطلاع دینا**; بھیجنا → **ارسال کرنا**; مدد → **تعاون**; سوچنا → **غور کرنا**. For yourself, humble words (**گزارش ہے کہ…** 'I request that…'); for the other person, honorific ones (**فرمائیے**).

**4. Letters and formal emails:** start **محترم / محترمہ** + name + صاحب / صاحبہ, make the request with **گزارش ہے کہ** + passive subjunctive (**مجھے چھٹی دی جائے** 'that leave be granted to me'), and close with **آپ کے تعاون کا شکریہ**. In practice most office email in Pakistan is in English; formal Urdu is for government offices, notices and some HR letters — but you will hear its phrases in speech all the time.

grammar.title: The passive: 'it was decided'
grammar.body:
**Form:** past participle (کیا، دیا، بھیجا، بتایا، بلایا…) + **جانا** in any tense:

کیا **جاتا ہے** 'is done' · کیا **گیا** 'was done' · کیا **گیا ہے** 'has been done' · کیا **جا رہا ہے** 'is being done' · کیا **جائے گا** 'will be done' · کیا **جائے** 'should be done / let it be done'.

**Agreement:** both the participle and جانا agree with the thing that undergoes the action: فیصلہ (m) کیا **گیا**; میٹنگ (f) ملتوی کی **گئی**; فائلیں (f pl) بھیجی **گئیں**. With کرنا the forms are کیا / کی / کیے. Add the helper دینا or لینا for a completed action: منظور کر **لی گئی** 'has been approved', ارسال کر **دی گئی** 'has been sent'.

**The person affected keeps کو**, and then the verb goes to masculine singular: آپ **کو** بتایا جائے گا 'you will be told', مجھے انٹرویو کے لیے بلایا **گیا** — even if 'I' am a woman.

**Who did it** is usually left out — that's the point: it sounds official and avoids blame. If you need it, use **کی طرف سے** 'from, on behalf of': کمپنی کی طرف سے.

**In everyday speech** people prefer the simple intransitive with **ہونا**: فیصلہ **ہو گیا** 'it's been decided', کام **ہو جائے گا** 'it'll get done', میٹنگ ملتوی **ہو گئی**. The passive is what you read in notices, emails and the news, and hear from officials, receptionists and HR.

culture:
Office Urdu in Pakistan is thoroughly mixed with English: **میٹنگ، ای میل، ڈیڈ لائن، رپورٹ، پریزنٹیشن** are the normal words, and whole sentences switch language halfway through. What doesn't switch is respect: seniors are **سر** and **میڈم** (even in English-speaking firms), get **آپ** and plural verbs, and are rarely called by their first name alone — **خان صاحب**, **قریشی صاحب**, **عائشہ میڈم**.

Tea is the glue of office life: the office boy brings chai round, and 'let's have tea' is how problems get sorted out. Friday has a long break for Jumu'ah prayers, and many offices close early on Fridays or work a half-day on Saturdays. Bosses are often added to WhatsApp groups, and messages to them open with **السلام علیکم سر** (often abbreviated 'AoA') and close with **شکریہ**.

**ان شاء اللہ** after a deadline is sincere, but it's also a running joke that it can mean 'probably not on time' — if you need a firm commitment, ask **پکا؟** 'definitely?'. In interviews, expect a mix of Urdu and English, answer seniors with **جی** before everything, and dress formally.

tip.body:
- A single respected person gets **plural** verbs, even when you talk *about* them: باس آ **گئے** ہیں, میڈم میٹنگ میں **ہیں**.

tip.title: By when? کب تک … ہو جائے گا
tip.body:
- **تک** after a time = **by** or **until**: جمعے **تک** 'by Friday'.
- **ہو جائے گا / گی** 'it'll get done' needs no doer; it agrees with the job: رپورٹ (f) ہو جائے **گی**.
- Promise with the helper **دینا**: بھیج **دوں گا** 'I'll send it off'. Everyone adds **ان شاء اللہ**.

tip.title: The passive: کیا گیا، دی گئی
tip.body:
- Past participle + **جانا**: فیصلہ کیا **گیا** 'it was decided', بتایا **جائے گا** 'will be told'.
- Both parts agree with the thing: میٹنگ (f) ملتوی کی **گئی**.
- With **کو** the verb stays masculine: آپ کو بتایا **گیا**.
- Who did it is left out — that's why notices and HR love it.
tip.pattern: participle + گیا / گئی / گئے · جائے گا

lessons.title: Asking for leave and writing to your boss

tip.title: Polite and formal: چاہیے تھی، گزارش ہے
tip.body:
- Soften a request with the **past**: مجھے بات کرنی **تھی** 'I wanted a word', مجھے چھٹی چاہیے **تھی**.
- In writing: start **محترم** …, ask with **گزارش ہے کہ** …, end **آپ کے تعاون کا شکریہ**.
- Formal swaps: بھیجنا → **ارسال کرنا**, بتانا → **آگاہ کرنا**.

میری طبیعت ٹھیک نہیں، آج میں گھر سے کام کروں گا۔
میں ای میل میں سب لکھ کر بھیج دیتا ہوں۔

lessons.title: The job interview

tip.title: Interview Urdu
tip.body:
- Everything in **آپ**, and start answers with **جی**: جی، مجھے تین سال کا **تجربہ** ہے.
- Experience: **X سال کا تجربہ** — کا, because تجربہ is masculine.
- Good news comes in the passive: آپ کو **منتخب کر لیا گیا ہے** 'you have been selected'.

new: آپ یہ نوکری کیوں چاہتے ہیں؟
